prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2025-10-30, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2025-10-30):
| Current ratio           | 1.27 |
| Retained earnings       | 17,093M |
| Current liabilities     | 28,136M |
| Current assets          | 35,630M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 18,552M |
| Total liabilities       | 78,289M |
| Total assets            | 96,889M |
| EBIT / operating income | 3,639M |
| Revenue                 | 12,222M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows solid profitability with EBIT margin near 30% on revenue, but very high leverage (total liabilities ≈ 78.3Bn vs equity ≈ 18.6Bn, D/E ≈ 4.2) and a modest current ratio (1.27), implying meaningful debt service and liquidity risk despite good earnings. Given strong earnings power yet elevated leverage, the issuer is best positioned at the investment-grade boundary, likely BBB+. 

DECISION: BBB+
